title: 5x5 grid r=0.09999 + central hole circle
abstract: 25 circles on a fixed 5x5 grid at {0.1,0.3,0.5,0.7,0.9} with radius r0=0.09999 to avoid numerical tangency; add one circle at (0.2,0.2) with radius sqrt(0.02)-r0-1e-6. Strictly non-overlapping and within bounds.

original_submission.content:
import numpy as np

def construct_packing() -> tuple:
    """
    Construct 26 circles in the unit square:
      - 25 circles: radius r0=0.09999 on a fixed 5x5 grid at coords {0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9}
      - 1 additional circle at (0.2, 0.2) with radius d - r0 - eps,
        where d is the distance to a neighboring grid center (0.1, 0.1)
    Returns:
        centers: np.ndarray (26,2)
        radii:   np.ndarray (26,)
    """
    r0 = 0.09999
    eps = 1e-6

    coords = [0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9]
    centers = [[x, y] for x in coords for y in coords]  # 25 grid centers
    radii = [r0] * 25

    # Hole circle at the center of a cell
    hole_center = np.array([0.2, 0.2], dtype=float)
    # Distance to one of the four nearest grid neighbors (e.g., (0.1, 0.1))
    neighbor = np.array([0.1, 0.1], dtype=float)
    d = float(np.linalg.norm(hole_center - neighbor))
    r_hole = d - r0 - eps  # strictly less than tangency to avoid numerical issues

    centers.append(hole_center.tolist())
    radii.append(float(r_hole))

    centers = np.array(centers, dtype=float)
    radii = np.array(radii, dtype=float)

    return centers, radii
